title: Coefficient/exponent pair (3, 1) for the fixed BK/Shoup affine-disperser family via self-contained gate elimination

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total BK/Shoup family defined in proof.md (identical to the starting seed's family): f_0=0; for n>=1 choose the least prime k>2*n^(3/5), r=ceil(n/k), t=ceil(sqrt(r)); fix one deterministic Shoup F_2 irreducible-polynomial algorithm; pad x with zeros into r field blocks, set y_i=phi_i(x)^(2^(i+1)-1), and output the constant coefficient of Sym_r^t(y_1,...,y_r). The fixed algorithm and field basis are as specified in proof.md.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"3"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"3"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one total uniform polynomial-time family, hence in NP with empty witnesses, C_B2(f_n)>=3n-4*floor(6*n^(4/5))-4 for every sufficiently large integer length n=|x| in the full Li\u2013Yang B2 model, so C_B2(f_n)>=3n-o(n). Proof: the Ben-Sasson\u2013Kopparty affine-disperser property (f_n nonconstant on affine subspaces of dimension >6n^(4/5)) plus a self-contained gate-elimination argument showing any B2 circuit for a function nonconstant on all affine subspaces of dimension >d has at least 3n-4d-4 gates.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}
